brief: c104, three manager passes old: the church's rose window has a two-sided dusk seam — the cached disc steps at cache time and the relight is a 0.7·nightF screen pass, so at the dusk hour the disc changes in a step while its glow ramps. #63 diagnosed it; nobody fixed it. Draw the disc live after applyLight (the ROSE relight pass is already there) so one 0..1 (nightF) sets both the disc and its glow, and remove the cached copy. Prove it with a dusk filmstrip crop on the tower (probes/filmstrip AT a dusk hour, pops.mjs graded against neighbours) and a gcv hash showing the ground cache is untouched. While there, fix the instrument in c116: fountain-freeze.mjs's summer identity half should hash gcv, not cv.
successLooksLike: A dusk filmstrip crop on the tower shows the rose window brightening in one smooth ramp with no step; the night wide shot is unchanged; ground rebuild count unchanged.
avoid: Do not touch the pane relight for the ordinary windows. Do not widen the crossfade past the threshold it already has (the staged-appearance law).
